title: In 1812, an Earthquake Made the Mississippi River Run Backwards

scenes.text: In 1812, an earthquake made the Mississippi River run backwards.
New Madrid, Missouri. Three quakes near magnitude 7.5 in two months.
The river bed heaved up. Water rushed upstream over a brand new waterfall.
The ground sank 20 feet and the river poured in, creating Reelfoot Lake.
Church bells rang in Charleston, 600 miles away. It was felt over a million square miles.
Reelfoot Lake is still there today. A lake made by an earthquake, in a place with no mountains.

description:
The New Madrid earthquakes of December 1811 to February 1812 in Missouri included three shocks of around magnitude 7.5 and briefly sent the Mississippi River flowing upstream where the fault lifted the river bed.
The ground sank by several metres in Tennessee and the river filled the hollow, creating Reelfoot Lake, which still exists. Shaking was felt over more than a million square miles and rang church bells in Charleston, South Carolina.
Did you know America's biggest quakes weren't in California? Comment below.
first_comment: The New Madrid fault is still active, and the area it shook was ten times bigger than the 1906 San Francisco quake. Would you build a house on it?
